Residual is a single adjacent-pair reorder in the case-7 loop preheader: target `mtctr r0; li r5,0; addi r4,r3,LO` vs ours `mtctr r0; addi r4,r3,LO; li r5,0`, with the base's `lis` HA already scheduled identically before `mtctr` in both. AXIS1 (hoist the table base into a named local `u8 *tbl` assigned AFTER `i = 0`, to force the index init to own the earlier IR node): REGRESSED real 2 -> 36, insns 104/102, multiset 2t -- naming the base let MWCC strength-reduce the `base + i` recompute into a moving pointer, DELETING both the per-iteration `add r3,r4,r5` and the preheader `li`; the named-base form is therefore incompatible with this loop's target shape and must not be retried. AXIS2 (split `i = 0` out of the for-header into its own preceding statement, keeping the base expression spelled inline in the body so the recompute survives): NEUTRAL, byte-identical, real 2, insns 104/104, multiset 0t -- splitting the for-init does not reorder the preheader nodes at all. Both probes reverted; tree restored to HEAD.
attributes.residual: SCHEDULE, one adjacent-instruction transposition, opcode multiset IDENTICAL. MECHANISM NAMED: MWCC emits the loop-invariant base-address `addi rBase,rHA,LO` (LICM-hoisted out of the loop body) BEFORE the loop's own index initialisation in the preheader, while retail emits the index init first. Neither instruction corresponds to a movable source statement -- the index init is a `for` header clause and the base materialisation has no source statement of its own -- so no statement-order lever exists to separate them, which is precisely why the reorder law does not reach it. CritterLoadStartNext carries the byte-identical residual at its own case-7 loop (target `li r5,0` / `addi r4,r3,LO` transposed, real 2, 108/108, frame 0x48, saves r24-r31); its loop body is a copy of this one, so any solution transfers to both at once and neither was re-probed separately.
